message:
QUESTION:
Did the new onboarding flow (launched 1 March) improve the budgeting app's month-3 retention, and by how much?

DATA:
Subscription budgeting app. A new onboarding flow went live on 1 March for all new sign-ups. Also on 1 March, the company completed its acquisition of a rival app, Tallyo. Tallyo's existing paying users were migrated into the product and counted as new sign-ups in the month they migrated (600 in March, 400 in April, none in any other month).

Monthly sign-up cohorts: users still active at the end of month 1, 2 and 3 after sign-up. Data extracted 1 August; '-' = not yet observable.

| Cohort | Sign-ups | M1 | M2 | M3 |
| Jan | 2,000 | 1,200 | 960 | 840 |
| Feb | 1,800 | 1,062 | 846 | 738 |
| Mar | 2,400 | 1,560 | 1,272 | 1,128 |
| Apr | 2,200 | 1,452 | 1,166 | 1,034 |
| May | 2,500 | 1,700 | 1,375 | - |
| Jun | 2,600 | 1,768 | - | - |

Migrated Tallyo users are included in the table above:
- March: 600 sign-ups; active M1 480, M2 450, M3 420.
- April: 400 sign-ups; active M1 320, M2 300, M3 280.

Month-3 retention (M3 / sign-ups) is the company's headline retention metric. No other product changes were made between January and June.

<analysis>
# Onboarding Flow: Retention Impact

*Based on the 1 August data extract. May–September M3 figures should now be observable; see "Before this goes to the board" below.*

## Question
Did the new onboarding flow, live for all new sign-ups from 1 March, improve month-3 (M3) retention? If so, by how much?

## Answer
**No measurable improvement. Organic M3 retention changed by −0.9 points (95% interval −3.2 to +1.3) in the first two post-launch cohorts.**

The reported lift of about 5.5 points comes from the Tallyo acquisition, not from onboarding. On 1 March, the day the flow launched, 1,000 existing Tallyo paying users were counted as new sign-ups: 600 in March and 400 in April. They retain at 70% at M3, against about 41% for organic sign-ups.

With migrated users removed:
- **January–February (pre-launch):** 41.5%
- **March–April (post-launch):** 40.6%

This rules out the reported 5–6 point lift. It cannot detect effects smaller than about 3 points in either direction (see "What this analysis can and cannot detect").

## Before this goes to the board
The extract is more than three months old. M3 for the May–September cohorts should now be available, so **refresh the data first**. The May and June cohorts, which show a large unexplained improvement (see below), are the most important to update. Presenting the 1 August numbers without that refresh will invite the obvious question.

## Why the reported number is misleading

| | Sign-ups | M3 active | M3 retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre (Jan + Feb) | 3,800 | 1,578 | 41.5% |
| Post, as reported (Mar + Apr, incl. Tallyo) | 4,600 | 2,162 | 47.0% |
| Post, organic (Mar + Apr, excl. Tallyo) | 3,600 | 1,462 | 40.6% |

Migrated Tallyo users retained at 80% / 75% / 70% at M1 / M2 / M3 in both months. They were already paying and engaged, so they are not comparable to people signing up cold. They made up 25% of the March cohort and 18% of the April cohort. That was enough to lift blended M3 to 47.0% in both months.

"No other product changes" does not rule this out. The acquisition changed *who is in the cohorts*, not the product, and it happened on the launch date.

Migrated users are excluded because they have no comparable pre-launch baseline, not because the flow could not have affected them. *[Confirm whether migrated users went through the new onboarding flow.]* Even if it reached them, their retention is driven mainly by their existing relationship with a budgeting product.

## Organic cohorts (Tallyo users removed)

| Cohort | Sign-ups | M1 | M2 | M3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 2,000 | 60.0% | 48.0% | **42.0%** |
| Feb | 1,800 | 59.0% | 47.0% | **41.0%** |
| Mar | 1,800 | 60.0% | 45.7% | **39.3%** |
| Apr | 1,800 | 62.9% | 48.1% | **41.9%** |
| May | 2,500 | 68.0% | 55.0% | not in extract |
| Jun | 2,600 | 68.0% | not in extract | not in extract |

## Effect at each milestone (organic, Mar+Apr vs Jan+Feb)

| Milestone | Pre | Post | Difference | Approx. 95% interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | 59.5% | 61.4% | +1.9 pts | −0.3 to +4.1 |
| M2 | 47.5% | 46.9% | −0.6 pts | −2.9 to +1.6 |
| **M3** | **41.5%** | **40.6%** | **−0.9 pts** | **−3.2 to +1.3** |

M1 is where an onboarding change should show up first. It shows a small positive signal that is not statistically distinguishable from zero, and it does not carry through to M2 or M3.

## What this analysis can and cannot detect
- **Minimum detectable effect is about 3.2 points.** With about 3,700 users per side, the comparison has 80% power to detect an M3 change of roughly 3.2 points at α = 0.05. "No measurable improvement" means no effect of that size. A real effect of 1–2 points could exist undetected.
- **The true uncertainty is wider than shown.** The intervals treat each user as independent. With only two cohorts on each side, cohort-to-cohort variation adds noise. Organic M3 ranged from 39.3% to 42.0% across the four cohorts. That 2.7-point spread is larger than the measured effect.
- **The baseline may be seasonal.** January and February sign-ups include New Year's-resolution users, whose retention may differ from spring sign-ups. This has not been tested. Last year's January–April cohorts, if available, would show whether spring cohorts normally retain differently.
- **The "organic" group may include Tallyo users.** Only *paying* Tallyo users were migrated. Free-tier or lapsed Tallyo users who signed up directly would count as organic. Matching sign-up emails or device IDs against the Tallyo user list would settle this.
- **Offsetting effects cannot be excluded.** A small onboarding gain could be masked by a simultaneous shift in organic user mix, and the reverse is also possible. A before/after design cannot separate these.

None of these change the main conclusion. A 5–6 point lift is far outside any plausible range.

## Open question: what happened in May and June?
May and June contain no migrated users, yet they look clearly different from every earlier cohort:

| | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Organic sign-ups | 2,000 | 1,800 | 1,800 | 1,800 | 2,500 | 2,600 |
| Organic M1 | 60% | 59% | 60% | 63% | 68% | 68% |
| Organic M2 | 48% | 47% | 46% | 48% | 55% | – |

**This is unlikely to be the onboarding flow alone.** March and April had the same flow and no comparable gain, and no product changes were made between April and May.

**Two things changed at once in May.** Organic sign-ups rose about 40% over March–April, and early retention rose sharply. Together these point to a change in *who is signing up*. Candidate causes:
- Tallyo users (free, lapsed or referred) signing up directly
- a new acquisition channel
- a post-acquisition marketing campaign

Seasonality is less likely. An interaction between the new flow and a new user mix is possible.

If May follows the historical M2-to-M3 ratio (0.86–0.875), its M3 would be about 47–48%. This is a benchmark for the data refresh, not an estimate of the onboarding effect.

## Recommendations
1. **Refresh the data before presenting.** Confirm whether the May/June improvement holds through M3 and whether it continues in July–September cohorts.
2. **Do not report an onboarding-driven retention lift.** The defensible statement is:
   > *"Excluding migrated Tallyo users, month-3 retention for the first two post-launch cohorts is unchanged at about 41% (−0.9 points). This rules out a lift of more than about 3 points. Later cohorts show stronger early retention, and we are investigating the cause."*
3. **Report migrated users separately from the headline metric.** Otherwise March and April will permanently overstate organic retention.
4. **Break down May onward by acquisition channel and sign-up source,** and match sign-ups against the Tallyo user list, before attributing the jump to any cause.
5. **Use a randomised holdout for future onboarding changes.** Giving a small share of new sign-ups the old flow is the only way to measure effects of 1–3 points reliably.

---

### Notes on this revision (not for the board version)
- All figures were rechecked against the source table. No numerical changes.
- Added: minimum detectable effect (≈3.2 pts), seasonality caveat, possible Tallyo contamination of organic sign-ups, the treatment of migrated users, and the cohort-spread-versus-effect point.
- Moved the data refresh to the top. It now leads both the document and the recommendations.
- Settled on "−0.9 points" throughout, and gave M2 an explicit interval.
- Removed the appendix listing corrections to the earlier draft. If anyone saw that draft, send them those corrections separately: the Tallyo confound was missed; the launch date was 1 March, not mid-March; May/June M1 was compared with pre-launch M3; and the 75% M1 projection and the "120 extra users/month" figure were withdrawn.
- One item needs confirming before circulation: whether migrated Tallyo users went through the new onboarding flow.
</analysis>

Produce the final version of this analysis.
